flags: the abstract's '50 mg groups with ... a loading dose' does not say which loading dose (200 or 100 mg) its -21.2 belongs to; flagged, not assigned
pmid:37777018 and pmid:39023568 are biomarker substudies; pmid:37917289 is pharmacokinetic; pmid:42081176 is an image-analysis tool; none reports a further treatment effect
the lesion-level values (pmc:PMC11258076) pool the three 50-mg arms as 'the 50-mg group' and use 90% confidence intervals
pmid:39304339 splits the 364 by Fitzpatrick skin type (247 types I-III, 117 types IV-VI) and reports the pooled 50-mg arms' placebo-adjusted F-VASI difference with 90% confidence intervals
pmid:39709084 compares the extension period's 43 patients on ritlecitinib + nbUVB with 187 on monotherapy; its abstract does not say how nbUVB was assigned and calls the analysis exploratory
in the extension, 9 of the 43 on nbUVB discontinued under an nbUVB-group-specific efficacy rule (>10% T-VASI improvement by week 12), so the observed-case means leave out those non-responders

quote: Thirty of group A patients were treated with oral prednisolone daily and thirty of group B patients were treated with oral dexamethasone pulse therapy weekly.Results: Out of sixty patients of vitiligo, maximum patients of both groups had progressive type of vitiligo.

quote: Total sixty patients of vitiligo were enrolled and 30 of group A patients were treated with low dose oral prednisolone (0.3 mg/kg body weight) daily and 30 of group B patients were treated with oral dexamethasone pulse therapy (10 mg per week) for 16 weeks.Results During 12 week follow-up, increased body weight, headache, dyspepsia and fatigue were more frequent in group A as compared to group B.

Similarly, in group A other side effects noted were acne (33.3%), mooning of face (26.6%), striae (26.6%), hypertrichosis 13.2%, purpura (6.7%) and among the female patients, menstrual abnormality (71.4%) whereas in group B, no patient developed these problems from baseline to follow- up period (p<0.05).Conclusion Low dose oral prednisolone was found to be associated with more adverse effects than oral  examethasone pulse therapy in treating vitiligo.
